headline: Proposed 16-story, 196-unit tower at 99 Lowell Street draws objections over lost parking at hearing.
summary: The tower would replace the city-owned Hartnett lot, which has about 205 parking spaces, with 196 apartments and up to 7,325 square feet of commercial space. The applicant's attorney said a three-story garage with about 305 spaces would be built, and an agreement with the city calls for replacement parking at the Pearl Street garage. Public speakers opposed the project, mainly over lost parking and the view of St. Joseph's Cathedral. The matter will be considered at a business meeting in two weeks, and three subdivision cases were continued to December 3.
decisions: Continued the S2026-5 subdivision at Wellington Road to December 3.
Continued the subdivision at 333 Coppas Avenue to December 3 after the motion carried.
Continued the S2026-7 subdivision at 1308 Wellington Road to December 3.
discussion: 99 Lowell Street tower: Public speakers opposed the 196-unit project, citing the loss of about 200 parking spaces at the Hartnett lot. They also raised concerns about access to churches, safety walking at night, and snow on sidewalks.

Hartnett lot sale: Speakers asked whether the lot had been sold and why there was no public hearing on the sale. Discussion noted that the board of Mayor and Aldermen decided to sell the lot and that the review here covers only this proposal.

Pine Street parking: Members asked about reducing Pine Street to one lane to add parking. The applicant said DPW did not favor it because of traffic volume and the safety of pulling out of angled spaces.

Wellington Road traffic: Residents raised safety concerns about the 16-lot subdivision adding traffic to Wellington Road and nearby side streets. The applicant's engineer said a traffic study found no adverse impact.
